In vitro development of the Autonomous Colonoscope Robot System (ACRS) for fully automated colonoscope insertion

Keiichiro Kume, Tatsuru Taira, Seigo Terao and Nobuo Sakai

Communications Medicine 6, Article number: 366 (2026)

Abstract

Background

In the field of colonoscopy, robotic systems have been developed to support or replace human operators due to a shortage of trained endoscopists.

Methods

ACRS was trained using insertion data obtained from an expert endoscopist operating a standardized colonoscopy training model.

Results

Of the automated insertions at Level 3 or higher, sixty two were classified as Level 4 and completed without manual assistance.

Conclusions

The autonomous colonoscope robot system demonstrated reliable insertion performance in controlled in vitro testing.

Plain language summary

This plain language summary explains why autonomous endoscopy tools may help hospitals support screening programs when trained specialists are limited.

Methods

After an overview of system hardware, the study evaluated automated insertions on a repeatable bench model with carefully controlled training patterns.

Training protocol

The training protocol used recorded movement histories, pressure feedback, and insertion trajectories collected from experienced operators over repeated sessions.

Manual and automated insertion times were compared with predefined success thresholds so that performance could be evaluated consistently across trials.

Statistical analysis focused on insertion completion, assistance frequency, and observed loop formation during the controlled evaluation period.
